Alongside the Mecca Defense Alliance linking Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan, Fidan promoted the Middle Corridor through the South Caucasus and a route from the Gulf to Europe through Iraq and Turkey.

The proposed India–Middle East–Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) would run from India through the Gulf, Saudi Arabia, and Jordan to Israel’s Mediterranean ports and on to Europe. Turkey and Syria are advancing an alternative from Jordan through Syria to Turkey, bypassing Haifa. Saudi Arabia, whose normalization talks with Israel have stalled, is also exploring a Syrian route.

The stakes go beyond transit fees. An Israeli gateway would give regional governments an economic reason to cooperate with Israel. A Syrian-Turkish route would shift that incentive to Damascus and Ankara and weaken Israel’s leverage over trade between the Gulf and Europe.

Fidan frames the corridors as regional resilience. In practice, Ankara is working to make more of the region’s decisions possible without Israel, starting with where its freight goes.
